Fifty years after Mao's death, China still grapples with his legacy
subhead: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (1/7). Mao Zedong, who died on September 9, 1976, founded the People's Republic of China and still casts a shadow over the country's political life. The Chinese Communist Party, whose power base Mao established, remains divided between loyalty to his myth and condemnation of his 'mistakes,' which led to the deaths of tens of millions of people.

title: In this French city, social diversity in schools has almost disappeared
subhead: According to studies, the southern city of Perpignan is the most educationally segregated in France. It's divided between private schools, which rank among the most privileged in the country, and public schools, which, in almost every case, sit at the exact opposite end of the social scale.

title: Mario Draghi, the 'sphinx' still shaping the EU's agenda
subhead: At 79, the former president of the European Central Bank, who no longer holds any official office, remains at the heart of European Union politics. Elusive and deliberately secretive, he skillfully leverages his ability to speak to political leaders, business executives, and financial markets alike.
